key_insight: OmniStream introduces a single streaming visual backbone that fuses causal spatiotemporal attention with physically structured representations to perceive, reconstruct, and act in real time from continuous visual input.
problem_solved: Current vision foundation models are fragmented—specializing in static image semantics, offline temporal modeling, or separate spatial geometry—limiting their use for real-time agents that need causal, physically grounded representations from streaming data.
method: Design a unified, online-capable backbone that applies causal spatiotemporal attention to process continuous visual streams with low latency.
Jointly train objectives across perception, reconstruction, and action to produce shared, generalizable representations.
Incorporate geometry-aware/physically structured modules and efficient state-update mechanisms to support reconstruction and downstream control in streaming settings.
impact: OmniStream enables practical real-time visual agents by replacing brittle, task-specific stacks with one streaming backbone—reducing latency and engineering complexity while improving robustness across perception, 3D reconstruction, and action tasks.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: streaming backbone with causal spatiotemporal attention and geometry-aware modules (showing data flow and state updates).
Pipeline schematic: continuous input → shared representation → perception / reconstruction / action branches.
Evaluation chart: latency vs. task performance comparison between OmniStream and specialized baselines.
Timeline visualization: online processing window and memory/state update across frames (illustrating causality).
paper_title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
paper_authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
